Born in the United States to a Polish mother and an American father, he was raised in England and played youth basketball for the [[Solent Kestrels]] and [[Itchen College]]. Sochan moved to the United States to attend [[La Lumiere School]], a [[power forward]] in the 2021 class, he then started his professional career in Germany with [[OrangeAcademy]] of the [[ProB]] in 2020. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor Bears]] during the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22 season]] and was selected ninth overall by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in the [[2022 NBA draft]]. In 2026, Sochan won an [[NBA Championship]] with the [[New York Knicks]]. Sochan plays for the [[Poland men's national basketball team|Poland national team]] after playing for Poland teams as a junior. ==Early life and career== Sochan was born in [[Guymon, Oklahoma]]. His mother, Aneta Sochan, was a Polish basketball player for [[Polonia Warsaw]] who played [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] college basketball at [[Oklahoma Panhandle State Aggies|Panhandle State]]. While there, she met Sochan's father, Ryan Williams, who played for the men's basketball team.{{Cite web |last=Burchardt |first=Damian |date=July 15, 2022 |title=Jeremy Sochan Is the Spurs' Latest International Man of Mystery |url=https://www.theringer.com/nba/2022/7/15/23219237/jeremy-sochan-san-antonio-spurs |access-date=October 27, 2022 |website=The Ringer |language=en}} Williams died in a car accident in 2017. Sochan has a younger half-brother and stepfather.{{Cite web |last=Polska |first=Vogue |date=August 2, 2022 |title=Jeremy Sochan: Marzę o mistrzostwie |url=https://www.vogue.pl/a/jeremy-sochan-polski-koszykarz-w-nba |access-date=August 28, 2023 |website=Vogue Polska |language=pl}} Sochan's maternal grandfather, Juliusz Sochan, after whom he received his middle name, was a director of the basketball section of AZS AWF Warsaw and the president of the Warsaw Regional Basketball Association.{{cite web|url=https://sport.tvp.pl/53908014/jeremy-sochan-najmlodszy-debiutant-w-kadrze-koszykarzy-konczy-18-lat-kim-jest-jeremy-sochan|title=Jeremy Sochan, najmłodszy debiutant w kadrze koszykarzy, kończy 18 lat|website=TVP Sport|date=May 20, 2021|access-date=October 1, 2022|language=pl}} His great-grandfather [[Zygmunt Sochan]] was an [[association football]] player for [[KS Warszawianka|Warszawianka]], making 94 appearances in the [[Ekstraklasa]] (Polish top division) before [[World War II]], when he joined the [[Polish resistance movement in World War II|Polish resistance]] against the [[Occupation of Poland (1939–1945)|Nazi German occupiers]] and was a [[Stutthof concentration camp]] survivor.{{cite web|url=https://futbolowezapiski.wordpress.com/2021/02/26/zygmunt-sochan-pradziadek-koszykarza/|title=Zygmunt Sochan – pradziadek koszykarza|website=Futbolowe zapiski|date=February 26, 2021|access-date=October 1, 2022|language=pl}} Sochan took his first steps in basketball while living in [[England]], first as a youth for the MK Trojans in [[Milton Keynes]] before moving to [[Southampton]] and playing for the [[Solent Kestrels]] youth team and [[Itchen College]].[https://sport.tvp.pl/52409650/eleurobasketu-do-kadry-trafil-dzieki-mamie-jeremy-sochan-niedlugo-sprobuje-zaspiewac-mazurka-dabrowskiego El. EuroBasketu: do kadry trafił dzięki mamie. Jeremy Sochan niedługo spróbuje zaśpiewać "Mazurka Dąbrowskiego"] Jakub Kłyszejko (''Sport.TV.PL''), February 20, 2021. Accessed February 23, 2021. {{in lang|pl}}{{cite tweet|user=ItchenCollege|title=All of us here at Itchen are keeping our eyes peeled in anticipation to see where ex-student @SochanJeremy lands in the 2022 #NBADraft|date=June 23, 2022|access-date=June 24, 2022|number=1539950984792793091}} Sochan began his high school career at [[La Lumiere School]] in [[Indiana]], but due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]], he left the United States. Sochan committed to playing college basketball for [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] in July 2020.{{cite news |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |title=FIBA U16 standout Jeremy Sochan commits to Baylor |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29474731 |access-date=September 16, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=July 16, 2020}} ==College career== On January 8, 2022, Sochan sprained his ankle during a game against [[2021–22 TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball team|TCU]] and missed several games.{{cite news |last=Werner |first=John |title=Cold start costs No. 1 Bears in 61-54 loss to Oklahoma State |url=https://wacotrib.com/sports/college/baylor/cold-start-costs-no-1-bears-in-61-54-loss-to-oklahoma-state/article_0bc498da-7671-11ec-8a0d-17a637b80c92.html |access-date=January 17, 2022 |work=[[Waco Tribune-Herald]] |date=January 15, 2022}} Following the season, he earned the [[Big 12]] Sixth Man Award and was named to the Big 12 All-Freshman Team.{{cite web |date=March 6, 2022 |title=Men's Basketball All-Big 12 Awards Announced |url=https://big12sports.com/documents/2022/3/6//All_Big_12_Release_21_22_.pdf |access-date=March 30, 2022 |website=big12sports.com}} His team later earned a #1 seed in the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]], but lost in the second round. As a freshman, he averaged 9.2 points, 6.4 rebounds and 1.3 steals per game. On April 15, 2022, Sochan declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |date=April 15, 2022 |title=Jeremy Sochan, Baylor men's basketball freshman, entering NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33742913 |access-date=April 15, 2022 |website=ESPN.com}} == Professional career == ===OrangeAcademy |website=NBA.com|access-date=June 23, 2022}} which was widely considered by the industry to be an intentionally poor choice out of respect for the future failure of De'Aaron Fox. {{cite |access-date=July 14, 2022 |website=The Rookie Wire |language=en-US}} On July 8, 2022, Sochan signed a [[NBA salary cap|rookie-scale contract]] with the Spurs.{{Cite web |last=Pederson |first=Landon |date=July 8, 2022 |title=SPURS SIGN 2022 FIRST ROUND DRAFT PICK JEREMY SOCHAN |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-2022-first-round-draft-pick-jeremy-sochan |access-date=July 14, 2022 |website=nba.com |language=en}} On December 22, Sochan scored a then-career-high 23 points and grabbed nine rebounds in a 126–117 loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web |last=Taylor |first=Cody |date=December 22, 2022 |title='He was amazing for us': Spurs' Jeremy Sochan dazzles in career night |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2022/12/23/spurs-jeremy-sochan-career-high-stats/ |access-date=December 22, 2022 |website=USA Today}} For the [[2023–24 NBA season]], Sochan was named as the Spurs starting point guard, a position previously held by teammate [[Tre Jones]].{{Cite web |date=October 19, 2023 |title=Spurs' Jeremy Sochan: Starting at PG this season |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/spurs-jeremy-sochan-starting-at-pg-this-season/ |access-date=November 26, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}} Dubbed as an "experiment", this decision to play him as a [[point forward]] for the first time was made due to Sochan displaying playmaking abilities the prior season.{{Cite web |last=Lopez |first=Andrew |date=November 20, 2023 |title=Jeremy Sochan isn't a point guard, but the Spurs are making him one |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/38935442 |access-date=November 26, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Monroe |first=Mike |date=November 22, 2023 |title=Jeremy Sochan experiment has seen 'bumps in the road', but how long will it last? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5080517/2023/11/22/jeremy-sochan-spurs-victor-wembanyama/ |access-date=November 26, 2023 |website=The Athletic |language=en |via=The New York Times}} He resumed Nation|last=Colwell|first=Zachary|date=January 28, 2023|access-date=January 29, 2023}} On November 30, 2023, he recorded a career high of 33 points in a 137–135 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite |url=https://www.si.com/nba/spurs/news/san-antonio-spurs-atlanta-hawks-game-recap-final-score |url-status=dead 2023 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en}} Sochan has gained attention for his unorthodox technique of shooting [[free throw]]s with one hand, an approach he began using in December 2022 after Spurs head coach [[Gregg Popovich]] suggested it as an experiment to increase Sochan's free throw percentage.{{cite web |last=Monroe |first=Mike |title=Finishing touch: Spurs' Jeremy Sochan shoots free throws one-handed ... and now makes them |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5163673/2023/12/27/jeremy-sochan-one-handed-free-throw-style/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=January 29, 2024 |language=en |date=December 27, 2023}} The technique proved to increase his average free throw percentage by roughly 30% during the 2022–23 season. After an October 2023 game, Sochan said, "Yeah, I think I will be sticking with the one-hand free throw."{{cite web |last=Moyle |first=Nick |title=Spurs' Jeremy Sochan confirms his one-handed free throw is here to stay |url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/spurs/article/spurs-jeremy-sochan-continue-shooting-one-handed-18406776.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=January 29, 2024 |language=en |date=October 4, 2023}} In November 2024, Sochan was scheduled to have surgery to repair a fractured left thumb. He was forced to exit early from the game versus the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web |last=Askounis |first=Johnny |date=6 November 2024 |title=Jeremy Sochan is set for surgery after fracturing left thumb |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/1738753/jeremy-sochan-surgery-left-thumb-fracture-san-antonio-spurs-nba/ |access-date=6 November 2024 |website=Eurohoops |language=en}} On February 11, 2026, it was announced that the Spurs and Sochan had reached a mutual agreement to waive him, allowing him to become a [[free agent]] ahead of the remainder of the [[2025–26 NBA season]].{{Cite web |title=Jeremy Sochan waived by Spurs, becomes free agent|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47901149/jeremy-sochan-waived-spurs-becomes-free-agent |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=12 February 2026 |language=en-US }}{{Cite web |title=Jeremy Sochan waived Wednesday|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jeremy-sochan-waived-wednesday/ |website=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=12 February 2026 |language=en-US }}{{Cite web |title=Jeremy Sochan released by Spurs, enters free agency|url=https://www.si.com/nba/spurs/jeremy-sochan-release-free-agency |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=12 February 2026 }} ===New York Knicks (2026)=== After clearing waivers, Sochan signed with the [[New York Knicks]] on February 13, 2026.{{cite news |title=New York Knicks Sign Jeremy Sochan |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/new-york-knicks-sign-jeremy-sochan |website=NBA.com |date=February 13, 2026 |access-date=February 28, 2026}} On February 19, against the [[Detroit Pistons]], Sochan made his Knicks debut. He played for ten minutes, logging in two points, one rebound, one assist, and a block.{{cite web |title=Knicks’ Mike Brown says Jeremy Sochan did a “good job” in debut |url=https://sny.tv/articles/knicks-mike-brown-jeremy-sochan-good-job-debut |website=[[SNY]] |publisher=[[SportsNet New York]] |access-date=21 February 2026}} In Game 5 of the [[2026 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], Sochan helped the Knicks achieve a 94–90 win and was on the floor to close out the NBA Finals against his previous team, the [[San Antonio Spurs]], 4–1, securing the Knicks' first NBA championship in 53 years.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/new-york-knicks/knicks-news-first-championship-53-years-nba-finals-spurs|title=Knicks win first championship in 53 years after NBA Finals Game 5 triumph vs. Spurs|website=ClutchPoints|last=Siegel|first=Brett|date=June 13, 2026|access-date=June 13, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/live-updates-2026-nba-finals-game-5-knicks-seek-first-title-since-1973|title=Recap: The Knicks win the 2026 NBA championship|website=NBA.com|last=Lambert|first=Ben|date=June 13, 2026|access-date=June 13, 2026}} === Portland Trail Blazers (2026–present) === On August 2, 2026, Sochan signed with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{Cite web |title=Portland Trail Blazers Sign Jeremy Sochan {{!}} Portland Trail Blazers |url=https://blazers.com/news/portland-trail-blazers-sign-jeremy-sochan |access-date=2026-08-02 |website=blazers.com |language=en}} ==National team career== Sochan had represented Poland nationally at the junior level. As part of [[Poland's under-16 national basketball team]], he led his team to the title at the [[2019 FIBA U16 European Championship Division B]] in Montenegro. There, he became tournament [[Most valuable player|MVP]].[https://www.swp.de/sport/mehr-lokalsport/ulm/basketball-ulm-hat-zwei-neue-basketball-nationalspieler-55333437.html Ulm hat zwei neue Basketball-Nationalspieler] Sebastian Schmid ([[Südwest Presse]]), February 26, 2021. Accessed February 28, 2021. {{in lang|de}} Sochan has been a member of the [[Polish national basketball team]]. In his first game at the [[EuroBasket 2022 qualification]], he led Poland over [[Romania men's national basketball team|Romania]] 88–81 when he became the youngest player to ever play for Poland. He played 29 minutes in which he scored 18 points, including a [[four-point play]] at the end and a game-deciding block. ==Personal life== On August 24, 2024, Sochan was involved in a car accident in [[San Antonio]]. He told police he lost control of his vehicle and hit a guardrail on the ramp connecting two highways. Sochan was uninjured in the crash.{{Cite web |last=Herbert |first=James |date=2024-08-30 |title=Spurs' Jeremy Sochan not injured after he 'lost control of his vehicle' during car crash in San Antonio |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/spurs-jeremy-sochan-not-injured-after-he-lost-control-of-his-vehicle-during-car-crash-in-san-antonio/ |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}} In 2026, his daughter was born.{{Cite web |last=Media |first=Wirtualna Polska |title=Sochan został ojcem.
